cpu_overheads_us.note: A55 is measured on the i.MX95. A78 and Kryo_Gen6 are scaled from it rather than invented independently, because the three costs are made of different things and a bigger core does not speed them up equally. dispatch is almost entirely kernel scheduler code plus a register save and restore, so it scales close to the core's integer throughput and a wide out-of-order core cuts it most. wake adds exiting an idle state, part of which is hardware sequencing that does not get faster with a wider pipeline, so it improves less. preempt is dominated by refilling cache and TLB after another task has run, and a bigger core has both a deeper pipeline to flush and more state to reload, so it improves least of the three. A78 is out-of-order and several times wider than the in-order A55; Kryo_Gen6 is a later ARM-derived core, taken as slightly ahead of A78. Within every CPU the order preempt > wake > dispatch holds, which is what the mechanism says it should be.
